title: Reranking: Precision at the Top
objective: After this lesson you will be able to place rerankers correctly in the funnel (cheap recall → precise rerank → minimal context), fuse cross-encoder scores with retrieval ranks, enforce top-k discipline under cost, and ablate the rerank stage to prove it earns its latency.
why: First-stage retrieval optimizes recall (don't miss); generation needs precision (top-5 must be right). Rerankers (cross-encoders scoring query+document pairs jointly) close that gap — at 10–100x the per-pair cost of bi-encoders. Misplaced (reranking 500) or missing (generating from raw recall) both waste the budget. Position and proof are the lesson.

blocks.text: First-stage retrievers encode query and docs **separately** (fast, precomputable, coarse): bi-encoder vectors, TF-IDF lists. **Rerankers** (cross-encoders) score each query+document **pair jointly** — full attention between them, far sharper relevance, far pricier per pair. The funnel exploits both: cheap systems gather 200 candidates, the reranker orders the top 50, generation reads 5. Cost tiers match precision tiers.

blocks.caption: k-bounds at every stage: recall breadth, rerank depth, generation focus

blocks.text: Fusing rerank scores with retrieval ranks

Reranker scores and retriever ranks disagree routinely — fuse, don't replace: weighted combination or RRF over both orderings (Ch.4 machinery reused). Pure reranker order ignores recall diversity (near-duplicate top-5); pure retrieval order wastes precision spend. Fusion weights are tuned on gold, not defaulted — and re-tuned when corpora shift.

Generation context holds **5±2 chunks**: more dilutes attention (lost-in-the-middle), costs linearly, and invites contradiction. If answers need more than 5 chunks, the problem is retrieval/chunking (too fragmented), not context size — fix upstream. Top-k is a quality control, not a truncation artifact.

blocks.title: Enforce the funnel
blocks.note: Run it: expect c2,c4 — recall order ignored, rerank scores rule, top-2 only. Then raise kGen to 6 and note nothing changes past available candidates: bounds cap spend, never pad.

items: Funnel tiers: cheap union recall (200) → precise rerank (50) → minimal generation (5), k-bounded each
Fuse rerank scores with retrieval ranks (RRF reuse); tune weights on gold
Top-k discipline: >5 chunks signals upstream (chunking/retrieval) failure, not context shortage

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice funnel and confirm c2,c4 top-2. (b) Change scores so c6 wins outright; state what changed downstream (generation context swaps). (c) Argue for kRerank=50 vs 200 in cost terms (relative rerank calls) and state the ablation that would settle it.
hints: Baseline: rerank order c2(0.9), c4(0.8), c6(0.7), c3(0.5) → top-2 c2,c4 regardless of recall order.
c6 to 0.95: top-2 becomes c6,c2 — generation context swaps one chunk; downstream answer may flip on that swap.
50 vs 200: 4x rerank calls. Ablation: gold hit-rate at top-5 for both settings — keep 200 only on measured gain.
exercise.why: Rerank mechanics (order override), context propagation (top-k swaps change answers), and cost ablation (settings earn latency) are the three rerank judgments — each computed on the toy, applied to production.
exercise.code: // Funnel-probe pattern: vary scores/k, watch generation-context swaps.

options: Budget blowout: rerankers cost 10–100x per pair — bound to top-50 after cheap recall; unspent precision budget is waste
quiz.explain: Cost tiers exist because precision is pricey. k-bounds match spend to stage value; unbounded reranking burns budget for flat gains.

options: Attention dilution + linear cost + contradiction risk: >5 signals upstream (chunking/retrieval) failure to fix instead
quiz.explain: Top-k discipline: context beyond ~5 degrades focus and grows cost. Fragmented needs mean chunk/retrieval redesign, not bigger windows.

quiz.q: Reranker disagrees with retriever order. Resolve by…
options: Fuse (RRF/weighted) with weights tuned on gold — disagreement is information from complementary scorers
quiz.explain: Complementary scorers disagree productively: lexical vs joint-attention signals fuse better than either alone — tuned, not defaulted.

summary: Cheap recall, precise rerank (k-bounded), minimal generation context — fused, ablated, disciplined. Precision positioned where it pays.
next: Ordered candidates in hand — now generate answers that stay honest: citations, abstention, and staleness guards. Next: grounded generation.
